assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised with sub-1e-18 fractional uncertainty, are a textbook case of a measurement technique that moves the limit of what can be observed: redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches. As an experimentalist who thinks in linewidths and systematic budgets, this is the strongest case on the list.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first Sr demonstrations; Ye's JILA group brought the clock to the lowest systematic uncertainties and many-body clock physics. The two-name configuration is clean, and the list contains no other credited person needed for the core idea.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent labs (Tokyo, JILA, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, others) confirm performance and the community is moving toward a redefinition of the SI second. Timely, with Hall and Hansch (frequency combs) already recognised and the clock application now delivered.
uncertainties: Hall and Wineland-era clock work overlaps, so the boundary against earlier prizes needs care.
Other contributors (e.g. Katori's collaborators on early Sr/Yb lattice work, and ion-clock groups) are not in the credited names, so fairness of the two-name split is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single colour-centre spins (notably NV centres in diamond) created a platform that works at room temperature and doubles as a nanoscale quantum sensor, with uses in magnetometry, thermometry and biology. This combines quantum-information interest with genuinely new measurement capability.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated optical detection of single NV spins and their coherent control; Awschalom extended the platform to broader defect spin systems (SiC, diamond) and coherence engineering. Lukin is a major figure but the field has more claimants than three slots, so the allocation is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature for sensing and spin control, with many independent groups, while the quantum-network side is still developing. Recognition is plausible now, though the breadth makes the specific discovery less sharp.
uncertainties: Compound field: single-spin detection, sensing, and defect-based qubits may merit different recognition.
Credit among Wrachtrup, Jelezko, Awschalom, Lukin and others (Hanson, Childress, Hollenberg, Wrachtrup/Jelezko timing) is not settled by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model with exquisite control and then opened quantum simulation, including superfluid-to-Mott transitions and single-site imaging. Measurement-driven in spirit, with a lasting influence on many-body physics and atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch) supplied the proposal for Bose-Hubbard physics in lattices; Bloch led the decisive experimental realisations and subsequent quantum-simulator programme. Greiner's quantum-gas microscope and Mott work is also important, so leaving him out is a real judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed across many labs, though quantum simulation is still evolving toward demonstrated advantage; timeliness is acceptable.
uncertainties: Overlap with B044, B005 and B031 candidates (Cirac and Zoller recur) means the prize framing could reorganise.
Greiner's omission and the experimentalist-versus-theorist balance are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is an invention built on engineered intersubband transitions, delivering mid-infrared and terahertz sources that underpin trace-gas spectroscopy, sensing and industrial use. A clear invention with demonstrable impact beyond physics, and a laser spectroscopist will value the tools it created.
assessment.attribution: The Bell Labs team (Faist, Capasso, Cho and colleagues, 1994) is the natural core; Cho's molecular beam epitaxy was necessary for the structure. Kazarinov and Suris proposed the underlying idea in 1971, who are not in the credited names, which complicates the credit story.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, widely commercialised and replicated, with decades of confirmation. Recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Prior theoretical proposal by Kazarinov and Suris is outside the credited names.
Whether the prize is more naturally an engineering award than physics is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire and SESAM mode-locking) enabled compact ultrafast sources that drive attosecond science, frequency combs, spectroscopy and imaging. A pure instrument contribution that opened new observational regimes.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed Ti:sapphire as a laser medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking, and Keller introduced SESAMs for self-starting and power-scaling. Credit is split among distinct complementary steps; the three-name configuration is plausible but not unique, and Spence's Kerr-lens analysis is another candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and ubiquitous in labs worldwide. Strickland and Mourou (CPA) and Krausz/Agostini/L'Huillier were already honoured, which makes the incremental novelty relative to earlier prizes a question.
uncertainties: Closeness to previous ultrafast and attosecond prizes.
Priority between Kerr-lens mode-locking authors and others not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates and Blatt's experimental implementations established trapped ions as a leading, high-fidelity quantum computing platform with outstanding coherence control.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller provided the 1995 proposal; Blatt delivered multiple key demonstrations (gate, teleportation, entanglement scaling). Wineland and Monroe are major experimental contributors, with Wineland already a laureate (2012) and Monroe not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally mature at small scale; scalability is still being proven, so some of the practical impact is still ahead. Timing is defensible but the recent 2025 superconducting-circuit prize may shape sequencing.
uncertainties: Monroe's omission and Wineland's earlier prize complicate attribution.
Cirac and Zoller overlap with B025 and B044, so only one such configuration is likely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned a foundations idea (no-cloning, entanglement) into a deployable technology with commercial and satellite demonstrations. Applied relevance is clear, and it connects to the entanglement-based tests already recognised in 2022.
assessment.attribution: BB84 (Bennett, Brassard) and E91 (Ekert) are the canonical protocols; Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known credit wrinkle. The three-name configuration is natural.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are decades old and experimentally demonstrated, but practical security (device imperfections, rates and distances) remains an open engineering issue, which tempers how decisive the physics impact is.
uncertainties: Real-world security and key rates remain limited; impact is partly speculative.
Wiesner's priority and relationship to B040 (long-distance communication) are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision full-sky measurements of the microwave background that fixed the cosmological parameters to percent level and established the lambda-CDM framework. It is a precision-measurement achievement with major field impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument scientist, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. The mission was a large collaboration, so a three-person limit leaves out many contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed independently by Planck. Cosmology prizes have recently gone to COBE (2006) and the 2011 and 2019 awards, so timing and novelty relative to those is uncertain.
uncertainties: Possible sense that the CMB theme has been recognised and that WMAP is incremental to COBE.
